title: Lottery and Egalitarian Funding Models Untested at Scale
bottleneck: Alternatives to peer review — funding lotteries among qualified proposals, or equal baseline grants to all qualified researchers — have theoretical and small-scale support but have never been tested at national scale. Calculations suggest egalitarian distribution could sustain current lab sizes, yet no major funder has committed to a real trial. Critics warn that lotteries could fund weak science and erode accountability, though evidence from small trials does not support these fears.
why_it_blocks: Without large-scale experiments, reform debates recycle the same untested arguments and the incumbent system persists by default.
current_state: New Zealand's Health Research Council and some private funders run small lotteries; no NIH/NSF-scale trial exists. A large, randomized trial of funding mechanisms would settle the debate but no funder has volunteered.
